assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mesoporous nanocrystalline TiO2 films sensitized with molecular dyes turned photoelectrochemical solar conversion into a practical, designable architecture, a materials concept where nanostructure, interfaces and molecular engineering jointly set function. It opened a whole field of molecular photovoltaics and was the conceptual precursor of perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the clear origin; Grätzel led the sustained development of the dyes, electrolytes and architecture. Hagfeldt is a major later contributor but the decisive credit rests with Grätzel and O'Regan; a two-person prize seems fair.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent confirmation, commercial niche products and wide use in photoelectrochemistry. Recognition is arguably overdue, though efficiency ceilings and displacement by perovskites reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views DSSC as a completed achievement or as superseded by perovskites.
Relative credit between O'Regan and Grätzel depends on supplied credit and my own recollection, which I have not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached silicon-competitive efficiencies in about a decade, an extraordinary change for photovoltaics, and they are a defect-tolerant, solution-processable crystalline semiconductor family with enormous structure-property richness. Impact on materials chemistry and energy research is very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers (2009), Park delivered the solid-state 2012 cell and Snaith the meso-superstructured/planar thin-film breakthroughs. Kanatzidis and Grätzel are significant but the first three give a coherent chain of discovery; credit is contested among many groups.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently and widely confirmed, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved. Recognition may be somewhat early relative to commercial maturity.
uncertainties: Operational stability and manufacturability remain open.
Contested priority and the many-contributor structure complicate a three-person limit.
Structural origin of defect tolerance and degradation mechanisms are still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture, organic structure-directing agents and tuned active sites underlies refining, petrochemistry and emission control (for example Cu-CHA for NOx). This is structure-function design realised at industrial scale, and the field is also near my own work, so I weigh the strength of structural proof carefully.
assessment.attribution: Corma's catalysis design, Davis's synthesis and mechanistic work, and Zones's structure-directing agent concept (SSZ-13 and related zeolites) are separate decisive threads. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are also important; the field is broad enough that a clean prize definition is hard.
assessment.maturity: Decades of deployment and confirmation. Timely given the prize on framework materials was recently awarded for MOFs, but the discovery is diffuse and the committee must define a specific advance, not just a field.
uncertainties: The discovery is a field with many contributors rather than one sharply defined result.
Possible overlap in the committee's mind with the recent MOF prize, and whether zeolite synthesis rather than discovery of new materials is the right crux.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C–N coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with exceptionally broad scope and robust ligand design. Its originality lies in transforming an inert bond formation into a general, predictable method.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general ligand-controlled methods and are consistently credited together. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, and a two-person prize is the clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of use and refinement, with exceptionally strong confirmation. Relation to the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be seen as an extension, which tempers urgency.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Kosugi's precedence is not fully resolved in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes created a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable surface chemistry and metallic conductivity, giving new structure-property combinations for energy storage, EMI shielding and catalysis. Characterising their atomic structure and terminations is difficult, which is exactly where structural evidence matters.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum jointly reported Ti3C2 in 2011 and built the field; the Drexel trio is a natural prize group. Barsoum's MAX phase foundation supports his role.
assessment.maturity: A little over a decade old with many independent groups, but applications are still developing and the true surface-termination structures are still debated. Probably somewhat early.
uncertainties: Surface terminations and stability are not fully settled.
Real-world applications are not yet established at scale.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts recast the active site of heterogeneous catalysts as isolated atoms, maximising atom efficiency and bridging homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis. This is a new conceptual framework, backed by aberration-corrected microscopy and X-ray absorption evidence.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Nature Chemistry paper by Qiao, Wang and Zhang, with Tao Zhang as leader, coined the field. Earlier work on isolated atoms (Datye, Liu and others) complicates credit and the choice of laureates.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well confirmed in many cases, but industrial use is limited and single-atom identification can be ambiguous. Recognition could be early.
uncertainties: Single-atom assignment and stability under reaction conditions are not always demonstrated.
Priority conflicts with earlier isolated-atom studies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated mesoporous silica (M41S/MCM-41, then SBA-15) created ordered materials with tunable 2-30 nm pores, enabling catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting of other materials. It is a landmark of the porous-materials field with clear structural characterisation.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck led the 1992 Mobil work, Stucky and Zhao extended it to SBA-15 and wide pore control, and Ryoo and Inagaki extended it with related materials. Parallel FSM-16 work in Japan complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and used, but the commercial impact has been more limited than anticipated. Timeliness is uncertain since many views might see the contribution as superseded by MOFs and zeolites.
uncertainties: Priority issues with parallel Japanese FSM-16 work and whether the prize should cover that.
Practical impact relative to the scientific influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals, diffraction-before-destruction, and time-resolved studies of reactions. It extends the crystallographic method to samples that conventional diffraction cannot handle, a point close to my own interests in nanocrystal methods.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 first demonstration with Fromme's photosystem I nanocrystals, and Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction concept. Schlichting is also important for time-resolved work, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: The method is validated, but the number of facilities is limited, and impacts on mechanism studies are still maturing. Possibly early, and the chemistry content may be less central than physics or biology.
uncertainties: Selection among four credited names is difficult.
Access constraints and limited number of broadly transformative structures so far.
Whether the committee sees it as chemistry.
